cases.sentence: Кутузов отступил к Вене, уничтожая за собой мосты на реках Инне (в Браунау) и Трауне (в Линце). 23-го октября ___ переходили реку Энс.
cases.explain: «русские войска» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Kutúzov fell back toward Vienna, destroying behind him the bridges over the rivers Inn (at Braunau) and Traun (near Linz). On October 23 the Russian troops were crossing the river Enns. At midday the Russian baggage train, the artillery, and columns of troops were defiling through the town of Enns on both sides of the bridge.

cases.sentence: Виднелся городок под ногами с своими ___ и красными крышами, собором и мостом, по обеим сторонам которого, толпясь, лились массы русских войск.
cases.explain: «белыми домами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: It was a warm, rainy, autumnal day. The wide expanse that opened out before the heights on which the Russian batteries stood guarding the bridge was at times veiled by a diaphanous curtain of slanting rain, and then, suddenly spread out in the sunlight, far-distant objects could be clearly seen glittering as though freshly varnished. Down below, the little town could be seen with its white, red-roofed houses, its cathedral, and its bridge, on both sides of which streamed jostling masses of Russian troops. At the bend of the Danube, vessels, an island, and a castle with a park surrounded by the waters of the confluence of the Enns and the Danube became visible, and the rocky left bank of the Danube covered with pine forests, with a mystic background of green treetops and bluish gorges. The turrets of a convent stood out beyond a wild virgin pine forest, and far away on the other side of the Enns the enemy’s horse patrols could be discerned.

cases.sentence: Виднелись башни монастыря, выдававшегося из-за соснового, казавшегося нетронутым, ___, и далеко впереди на горе, по ту сторону Энса, виднелись разъезды неприятеля.
cases.explain: «дикого леса» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Между орудиями, на высоте, стояли впереди начальник ариергарда генерал с ___, рассматривая в трубу местность.
cases.explain: «свитским офицером» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Among the field guns on the brow of the hill the general in command of the rearguard stood with a staff officer, scanning the country through his fieldglass. A little behind them Nesvítski, who had been sent to the rearguard by the commander in chief, was sitting on the trail of a gun carriage. A Cossack who accompanied him had handed him a knapsack and a flask, and Nesvítski was treating some officers to pies and real doppelkümmel. The officers gladly gathered round him, some on their knees, some squatting Turkish fashion on the wet grass.

cases.sentence: Офицеры радостно окружали его, кто на коленах, кто сидя по-турецки на ___.
cases.explain: «мокрой траве» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: — Да, не дурак был этот ___, что́ тут за́мок выстроил.
cases.explain: «австрийский князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, the Austrian prince who built that castle was no fool. It’s a fine place! Why are you not eating anything, gentlemen?” Nesvítski was saying.

cases.sentence: — Покорно благодарю, князь, — отвечал один из офицеров, с удовольствием разговаривая с таким важным ___.
cases.explain: «штабным чиновником» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Thank you very much, Prince,” answered one of the officers, pleased to be talking to a staff officer of such importance. “It’s a lovely place! We passed close to the park and saw two deer … and what a splendid house!”

cases.sentence: Мы мимо ___ проходили, двух оленей видели, и дом какой чудесный!
cases.explain: «самого парка» — after the preposition «мимо», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Thank you very much, Prince,” answered one of the officers, pleased to be talking to a staff officer of such importance. “It’s a lovely place! We passed close to the park and saw two deer … and what a splendid house!”

cases.sentence: — Нет, а чего бы я желал, — прибавил он прожевывая пирожок в своем красивом ___, — так это вот туда забраться.
cases.explain: «влажном рте» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “So they will,” said Nesvítski. “No, but what I should like,” added he, munching a pie in his moist-lipped handsome mouth, “would be to slip in over there.”

cases.sentence: Между тем ___, стоявший впереди, указывал что-то генералу; генерал смотрел в зрительную трубку.
cases.explain: «свитский офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Meanwhile the staff officer standing in front pointed out something to the general, who looked through his field glass.
